passage: Class teacher's note, Class 6. During today's Independence Day rehearsal, the flag went up and the anthem began. Madhav stood straight, arms at his sides, eyes on the flag. Beside him, Dhruv was poking the boy in front. Madhav said nothing during the anthem, but afterwards he told Dhruv, "My Dadaji says the anthem is 52 seconds. We can stand still that long." Dhruv shrugged, but in the second run-through he stood still. Madhav also offered to help the school helper fold the flag properly. I will ask him to lead the flag-folding team on the day.

qa.q: How long did Madhav say the anthem lasts?
qa.a: 52 seconds.

qa.q: Why did Madhav wait until after the anthem to speak to Dhruv?
qa.a: He respected the anthem too much to talk during it, and wanted to remind Dhruv without making a scene.

qa.q: Why is asking Madhav to lead the flag-folding team a good idea?
qa.a: It gives his respect for the flag a real role and lets him show others how to do it properly.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel after Madhav's comment?
qa.a: Maybe a little annoyed, but he stood still the second time, which suggests it made sense to him.

grounding: It shows, in a teacher's note, a boy honouring the flag and anthem and encouraging a classmate to do the same.

passage:
Diary, Thursday.
Our class visited the district court today. I thought it would be boring, but when the judge came in and everyone stood, I got goosebumps. Our guide said the building is 120 years old and belongs to all of us, so no scribbling on the benches. Vaibhav from my class tried to put his feet up in the waiting hall, and the guard told him off. I felt embarrassed for our school. At home I told Nanaji about it. He said that when he first voted, he wore his best shirt. I want to feel like that when I vote too.
- Madhuri

qa.q: How old is the court building, according to the guide?
qa.a: 120 years old.

qa.q: Why did Madhuri feel embarrassed when Vaibhav put his feet up?
qa.a: Madhuri felt the building deserved respect and that his behaviour reflected badly on their school.

qa.q: How could the teacher build on this visit?
qa.a: Ask the class to discuss why public buildings and institutions belong to everyone, and how to show respect in them.

qa.q: What does Nanaji's best-shirt story suggest about how he sees voting?
qa.a: He sees it as an important, proud moment worth dressing up for.

grounding: It shows a child feeling respect for a public institution and valuing an elder's civic pride.

passage: On Republic Day, rain had turned the village school ground into mud, but the whole village came anyway. Eshaan and Aadhya, both ten, had been chosen to carry the folded flag to the pole. Eshaan held it flat on his palms, wrapped in a plastic sheet so no drop would touch it. Aadhya walked beside him with an umbrella tilted over the flag, not over herself. When the sarpanch pulled the rope and the petals fell, Eshaan's grandfather, an old postman, saluted from under a sack. Afterwards Aadhya said, "My shoulders are soaked, but the flag is dry."

qa.q: What did Eshaan wrap the flag in?
qa.a: A plastic sheet.

qa.q: Why did Aadhya hold the umbrella over the flag and not herself?
qa.a: She cared about keeping the flag dry and respected, even more than keeping herself dry.

qa.q: How could the teacher recognise what the two children did?
qa.a: Thank them in front of the school for how carefully they carried the flag, so others see what respect looks like.

qa.q: How might Eshaan's grandfather feel watching his grandson carry the flag?
qa.a: Proud and moved, which may be why he saluted even from under a sack in the rain.

grounding: It shows village children honouring the national flag with care during a rainy Republic Day.

passage: On Monday mornings at their school in Cape Town, the flag went up while the anthem played through a crackly speaker. Thabo, ten, took off his cap and stood still, even though his shoelace was undone. Yara, who had arrived from Jordan in March, whispered, 'Why does everyone go so quiet?' Thabo waited for the last note. 'My gogo says it's for everyone who worked to make this country fair,' he whispered back. 'She was there when it changed.' Yara thought about it. At lunch she drew her own country's flag in her notebook and showed him. Thabo studied it carefully. 'Teach me what the colours mean,' he said, 'and I'll teach you the words of ours.'

qa.q: Where was Thabo's school?
qa.a: It was in Cape Town.

qa.q: Why did Thabo stand still even with his shoelace undone?
qa.a: He felt the anthem deserved his respect, partly because his gogo connected it with people who worked to make the country fair.

qa.q: How could a teacher build on the swap Thabo suggested?
qa.a: A teacher could invite children to share the flags and songs of their families' countries, so respect for symbols includes everyone's.

qa.q: What might the flag moment feel like for Yara as a newcomer?
qa.a: It may have felt confusing at first, then more welcoming once Thabo explained and asked about her own flag. 🤍

grounding: Shows a child honouring the national flag and anthem, linked to a grandparent's story, and respecting a classmate's flag too.

passage: The day before Republic Day, the scouts' room smelled of starch and marigolds. Arohi, twelve, and Gurpreet had been chosen to fold the flag so it would open cleanly at the ceremony. Gurpreet swung one corner round his shoulders like a cape. 'Superhero!' Arohi caught the cloth before it brushed the floor. 'Not on the ground. Sir said.' 'It's just practice.' 'Still.' She showed him how the petals go inside the last fold, the way the scout teacher had shown them, slowly, twice. Gurpreet stopped fooling and copied her. When the teacher checked, the bundle held. 'Good,' he said. 'Who noticed it nearly touched the floor?' Gurpreet, a little red, pointed at Arohi. 'She did.'

qa.q: What was placed inside the last fold?
qa.a: Petals were placed inside the last fold.

qa.q: How did Arohi feel when she caught the cloth so quickly?
qa.a: She felt protective of the flag and alarmed that it might touch the floor, since the teacher had said it must stay off the ground.

qa.q: What made Arohi's correction work?
qa.a: She did not scold; she showed him the proper fold slowly, which gave him a way to join in.

qa.q: What might Gurpreet have felt when he pointed at Arohi?
qa.a: Probably a bit embarrassed about his joke, but honest enough to give her the credit.

grounding: Illustrates a child treating the national flag with respect during a school ceremony rehearsal and following the school's rule.
